answer: Neighborhood pigment divergence. Each agent's neighborhood is the set of agents within two hops; a joining agent must match the pigment (a hash of its neighborhood's aggregate edge pattern) reported by most of its neighbors. Sybils created together share few real edges, so their pigment cluster is an oasis of near-identical hashes disconnected from the main graph and gets refused routing. An attacker must instead spread each fake identity across yarrow-diverse genuine neighbors, paying real interaction and latency costs per identity.
